about.author: The author
about.communityContributorDescription: contributed to the development and coding of the unofficial EDCH BGS / Manjaro extensions, including BGS tracking, patrols, French control labels and stability fixes.
about.bugsAreReportedGithubDebugLog: Bugs are reported on GitHub, with the debug log: it's what shows what happened.

about.buildExportFormatImportedIntoWishlist2: Build export format imported into the wishlist, and the Frame Shift Drive figures for the exact route (coriolis-data)

about.edchNotReplacementCommunitySOther: EDCH is not a replacement for the community's other tools. It is an independent project, unrelated to the projects listed below and to Frontier Developments.
about.edchWouldNotWorkWithoutThese: EDCH would not work without these projects, built and maintained by members of the community. Thanks to every one of them. If they are useful to you, please support them.
about.edengineerSEngineersDataGatheredCorrecte: EDEngineer's and the engineers' data, gathered and corrected, and the exobiology catalogue
about.eliteDangerousTrademarkFrontierDevelopme: Elite Dangerous is a trademark of Frontier Developments plc. The game's names and data belong to them.
about.engineeringRecipesMaterialOriginsPartTra: Engineering recipes, material origins and part of the translations
about.everySystemStationCommoditySearchRoutes: Every system, station and commodity search, and the routes (neutron, fleet carrier)
about.exobiologySpeciesNamesJournalWritesThem: Exobiology species names as the journal writes them
about.frameworkRunsAppWindows: The framework that runs the app on Windows
about.freeRelayCarriesWingSEncrypted: The free relay that carries the wing's encrypted messages
about.freeUnofficialNonCommercialCommunityTool: Free, unofficial and non-commercial community tool.
about.gameSOfficialIdentifiersNames: The game's official identifiers and names
about.gameSOfficialTranslatedNamesMaterials: The game's official translated names (materials, commodities, modules…)
about.inspirationEddnEdsmInaraSync: The inspiration for the EDDN, EDSM and Inara sync
about.lightweightCompanionEliteDangerousLiveIn: A lightweight companion for Elite Dangerous: live inventory, where to find every material, engineers, searches, navigation, controls and sync.
about.logPlainTextFileCanRead: A log is a plain text file: you can read it, and remove what you don't want to share, before sending it. A GitHub issue is public.
about.networkSharesGameDataBetweenPlayers: The network that shares game data between players. EDCH contributes to it.
about.neverApiKeysEdsmInaraQr: Never: your API keys (EDSM, Inara), the QR code's code, the wing code, your Windows user name or the path of your personal folder, your full IP addresses, your Wi-Fi's name, or the text you type. EDCH removes them from every line automatically, before writing it.
about.openIssueGithubExplainWhatWere: Open an issue on GitHub: explain what you were doing and what happened, then drag the file into the message.
about.openLogsFolderTakeNewestEdch: Open the logs folder and take the newest "edch-debug_…" file (and "edch-error_…" if there is one).
about.syncingFlightLogWhatCommunityKnows: Syncing your flight log, and what the community knows about the system you're in (Exploration)
about.thanksUsingEdchIfCrossPaths: Thanks for using EDCH! If you cross paths with MDLuffy out in the black, a little o7 is always welcome. Fly safe, Commander, and may your tanks always be full.
about.thenUntickDebugModeFileGrows: Then untick debug mode: the file grows quickly.
about.wasLargelyWrittenAiClaudeAnthropic: It was largely written by an AI (Claude, by Anthropic), overseen by a developer who decides the features, tests and approves every release. It may therefore be incomplete or contain bugs.
about.whatLogContainsNeverContains: What a log contains (and never contains)
about.yesEdchSVersionPagesOpened: Yes: EDCH's version, the pages opened and buttons clicked, errors, game events (systems, stations, missions, commodities), and commander names (yours and your wing's).
about.eddiTranslatedRanksStates: Translated names of faction states, ranks and some commodities

colonisation.constructionSitesTrackedFromJournalWhat: Construction sites tracked from your journal: what's left to deliver, your hold, trips and where to buy.
colonisation.dockFleetCarrierSquadronSTransfer: Dock at your fleet carrier (or your squadron's) and transfer goods: EDCH will follow its hold too. Your carrier's total comes from the carrier management screen.
colonisation.findWhereBuyNear: Find where to buy it near you
colonisation.gameJournalDoesnTListCarrier: The game journal doesn't list a carrier's hold: EDCH rebuilds it from your ship ↔ carrier transfers and your purchases and sales on its market. What others put in it, or what was there before your history starts (60 days), doesn't show. The carrier's market (what it sells with its stock, what it buys) comes from Spansh, checked again every 5 minutes: it depends on players who docked there. Inara doesn't let apps read a carrier's hold. Goods your construction sites need are highlighted.
colonisation.noConstructionProgressDockConstructionDe: No construction in progress. Dock at a construction depot (Colonisation): EDCH will read the list of commodities it needs.
colonisation.notEveryFeatureFullyWorkingYet: Not every feature is fully working yet. The game doesn't write a fleet carrier's content to the journal: its hold is an estimate, completed with the market as Spansh sees it. A connection to Frontier's API, which gives your carrier's full hold, is planned.

guide.checkTailscaleConnectedPcThenReopen: check that Tailscale is connected on the PC, then reopen the Remote access page.
guide.checkTailscalePhoneWindowsOpenWindows: check that Tailscale is on on the phone. In Windows, open Windows Security → Firewall & network protection → Allow an app through firewall, then tick EDCH for private and public networks (Tailscale is sometimes classed as "public").
guide.cutAccessUntickOptionTurnRemote: To cut access: untick the option, turn the remote access server off, or click "New code" to disconnect every device.
guide.donTGiveOtherPeopleAccess: Don't give other people access to your Tailscale account.
guide.downloadWindowsVersionRunSignTailscale: Download the Windows version, run it and sign in. The Tailscale icon next to the clock should say "Connected".
guide.edchDesignedUsedHomeNetworkGoing: EDCH is designed to be used on your home network. Going through the Internet isn't what it's meant for: remote access through Tailscale is for now the only alternative, while a solution built into EDCH is being developed. Only turn it on if you need it.
guide.fromPlayStoreAppStoreSign: From the Play Store or the App Store. Sign in with the same account and allow the VPN when the app asks.
guide.guestWiFiRepeaterSecondRouter: guest Wi-Fi, a repeater or a second router that keeps the phone away from the PC.
guide.hotelStationCafeEdchSLocal: in a hotel, a station or a café, EDCH's local connection isn't encrypted. With Tailscale, everything is encrypted.
guide.ifEliteDangerousEdchRunRemote: if Elite Dangerous and EDCH run on a remote PC (Shadow, Boosteroid…), your phone isn't on the same network. Tailscale links the two.
guide.installTailscalePcRunningEdch: Install Tailscale on the PC running EDCH
guide.neverShareQrCodeLinkThey: Never share the QR code or the link: they contain the secret code.
guide.pickTailscaleAddressEdch: Pick the Tailscale address in EDCH
guide.privateNetworkBetweenOwnDevicesEach: A private network between your own devices. Each one gets an address starting with 100. Connections are encrypted end to end and nothing is opened to the Internet: only the devices signed in to your Tailscale account can see each other. It's free for personal use. Tailscale is a service independent of EDCH.
guide.qrCodeShows192168Address: The QR code shows a 192.168… address:
guide.remoteAccessPageTurnRemoteAccess: On the Remote access page: turn the remote access server on, then pick "Tailscale" in the "PC address" list (the address starts with 100). The QR code and the link update by themselves.
guide.tailscaleComGoogleMicrosoftAppleGithub: On tailscale.com, with your Google, Microsoft, Apple or GitHub account.
guide.tailscaleTurnedPhoneDoneEdchOpens: With Tailscale turned on on the phone. Done: EDCH opens over Wi-Fi as well as 4G/5G.
guide.travellingWorkFollowMissionsWishlistWing: travelling or at work, you follow your missions, your wishlist or your wing on your phone over mobile data.
guide.wiFiEthernetAddressSelectedPick: the Wi-Fi or Ethernet address is selected: pick "Tailscale" in the "PC address" list. If Tailscale isn't in the list, it wasn't running when the page opened: open the page again.

mining.findsStationsSystemsControlledChosenPowe: Finds the stations in systems controlled by the chosen power (exploited, fortified or stronghold) that buy the mineral, sorted by price, and the rings with a hotspot of that mineral in those systems. Selling in one of your power's systems minerals mined in that same system earns merits. Spansh data.
mining.fireProspectorLimpetAsteroidCompositionW: Fire a prospector limpet at an asteroid: its composition will show here.
mining.liveProspectorResultsWhereMineSell: Live prospector results, and where to mine and sell to earn Powerplay merits.
mining.noHotspotsMineralSMinedLasers: No hotspots for this mineral: it's mined with lasers in rings of the right type (metallic for metals), without hotspots.
mining.noKnownBuyerWithinLyLl: No known buyer within {{MAXRADIUS}} ly. You'll have to go further, with a fleet carrier for example.
mining.noKnownHotspotWithinLyLl: No known hotspot within {{MAXRADIUS}} ly. You'll have to go further, with a fleet carrier for example.
mining.nothingWithinLyRadiusWidenedLy: Nothing within {{start}} ly: radius widened to {{radius}} ly. Plan a long trip, or move your fleet carrier.
mining.ringsHotspotChosenMineralNearestFirst: Rings with a hotspot of the chosen mineral, nearest first, then where to sell it at the best price. Radius: {{maxDistance}} ly, widened automatically if nothing is found. Spansh data.
mining.whenProspectorFindsOneTheseTargets: When a prospector finds one of these targets above the chosen percentage (or a core for deep mining), EDCH tells you with the sound and colour chosen in Settings → Notifications.
mining.whereMineSellPowerSSystems: Where to mine and sell in your power's systems
mining.hideMethod: Hide this mining type from the results
mining.showMethod: Show this mining type in the results
mining.noRingForShownMethods: No ring for the mining types shown: click a hidden type above to show it again.
mining.asteroidsShownHelp: How many of the last prospected asteroids to show

missions.eachKillCountsOneMissionPer: Each kill counts for one mission per issuing faction, so you need as many kills as the biggest stack.
missions.enterCreateCodeLeast8Characters: Enter or create a code (at least 8 characters) to join the wing.
missions.everyWingMemberUsingEdchEnters: Every wing member using EDCH enters the same code. The missions you choose to share are sent to the others, encrypted with this code, through the free ntfy.sh service: nobody else can read them.
missions.newCodeCreatedGiveOtherMembers: New code created: give it to the other members
missions.noActiveMissionsMissionsAcceptGame: No active missions. Missions you accept in game show up here, with their objective, destination and time left.
missions.noStationSellsWithinChosenRadius: No station sells {{commodityName}} within the chosen radius.
missions.notEveryFeatureFullyWorkingYet: The game logs missions you accept yourself and some cargo delivery events, but may not log receiving a wingmate’s shared mission. Confirm those missions manually below after accepting them in the game. Manual confirmations are declarations, not journal verification.
missions.manualConfirmationHelp: Only confirm after accepting in Elite Dangerous. The status is shared with wingmates using EDCH and can be revoked. It is not proof from the game.
missions.manualError: Unable to update: make sure the wing link is connected and a teammate is still sharing this mission.
missions.savedOfflineConfirmations: Saved confirmations without a currently visible mission (revoke them here):
missions.otherwiseShareEachMissionShareWing: Otherwise, share each mission with the "Share with the wing" button on its card. A mission a member shared that you accept is shared right away: the others see you took it.
missions.shareAllMyWingMissionsAutomatically: Share all my wing missions automatically
missions.whatNotifiesNewMissionAcceptanceMember: What notifies you (new mission, acceptance, a member leaving…) is set in
missions.whereGetBuyMine: Where to get it (buy or mine)

mobile.connectPhoneSameWiFiPc: Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi as this PC.
mobile.deviceConnectedEdchPcDataUpdates: This device is connected to EDCH on your PC. Data updates by itself.
mobile.linkContainsSecretCodeLikeQr: The link contains the secret code, like the QR code: only share it with your own devices.
mobile.linkCopiedContainsSecretCodeOnly: Link copied: it contains the secret code, only share it with your own devices
mobile.localConnectionIsnTEncryptedHttp: The local connection isn't encrypted (HTTP): use it on your home network, not on public Wi-Fi. Away from home or on public Wi-Fi, go through Tailscale (encrypted).
mobile.newCodeConnectedDevicesMustScan: New code: connected devices must scan again
mobile.newCodeDisconnectsEveryDeviceAlready: "New code" disconnects every device already authorised.
mobile.offDefaultAlsoServesOpenBrowser: Off by default. It also serves the "Open in the browser" page. Only devices that scanned the QR code can open the page: knowing the PC's address is not enough.
mobile.openEdchPhoneTabletAnotherScreen: Open EDCH on your phone, tablet or another screen (browser), on the same network as this PC.
mobile.phoneWishlistCanEditedSyncsPc: On the phone, the wishlist can be edited and syncs with the PC. Exports, imports and EDDN sync stay on the PC.
mobile.pickConnectionPhoneUsesReachPc: Pick the connection the phone uses to reach this PC: Wi-Fi or Ethernet at home, Tailscale from outside. The QR code and the link follow your choice.
mobile.scanQrCodeEdchOpensBrowser: Scan the QR code: EDCH opens in the browser and the device stays authorised.
mobile.tailscaleEncryptedPrivateNetworkBetweenO: With Tailscale, an encrypted private network between your own devices, free for personal use.
mobile.tailscaleIsnTDetectedPcFollow: Tailscale isn't detected on this PC. Follow the guide to install it, then come back to this page.
mobile.tailscaleRunningPcUsePickTailscale: Tailscale is running on this PC ({{ts}}). To use it, pick "Tailscale" in the "PC address" list above.
mobile.turnTailscalePhoneSameAccountPc: Turn Tailscale on on the phone (same account as on this PC). Wi-Fi or mobile data, either works.
mobile.windowsMayAskAllowEdchThrough: Windows may ask to allow EDCH through the firewall: accept for private networks.

navigation.autoCopyNextSystemOffSettings: Auto-copy of the next system: off (Settings → Game and search → Navigation)

navigation.fsdOptimalMassTTMax: · FSD {{value}} (optimal mass {{optimalMass}} t, {{maxFuelPerJump}} t max per jump)
navigation.gameHasnTSentShipS: The game hasn't sent your ship's loadout yet (Loadout event). Start the game or switch ships.
navigation.higherCloserRouteSticksStraightLine: The higher, the closer the route sticks to a straight line
navigation.intermediateRangesAreCalculatedFromGame: Intermediate ranges are calculated from the game value (official FSD formula).
navigation.maxLyPerJumpFilledFrom: Max {{CARRIERMAXJUMP}} ly per jump. Filled from the journal once you've opened carrier management.
navigation.neutronBoost6CaspianExplorerS: Neutron boost ×6 (Caspian Explorer's Mk II FSD)
navigation.noShipReadFromJournalYet: No ship read from the journal yet: start the game
navigation.reAboutTTritiumShortTank: You're about {{missing}} t of tritium short (tank + hold).
navigation.scoopHereFuelIsnTEnough: Scoop here: the fuel isn't enough for what follows without refuelling

navigation.spanshFoundNoRouteShipNot: Spansh found no route with this ship (not enough range or fuel?).
navigation.spanshPlotsShipFsdMassTanks: Spansh plots with your ship (FSD, mass, tanks): every jump is possible with the fuel left, and the route shows where to scoop.
navigation.spanshPlottingCarrierRoute: Spansh is plotting the carrier route…
navigation.spanshPlottingExactRouteFuelIncluded: Spansh is plotting the exact route (fuel included)…

navigation.theoreticalMinimumWithoutNeutronBoostsRe: Theoretical minimum without neutron boosts; the real route takes a few more jumps.
navigation.tritiumTankHoldEnoughEstimate: The tritium in the tank and hold is enough (estimate).

settings.appliesPhoneTooSettingsAboutAlways: Applies on the phone too. Settings and About always stay visible.
settings.checkGithubNewVersionsAutomatically: Check GitHub for new versions automatically
settings.clickingSystemAlsoOpensNavigationSystem: Clicking a system also opens Navigation, with that system as destination
settings.copyNextJumpAutomaticallyWhenI: Copy the next jump automatically when I arrive in a system of the route (Navigation page)
settings.debugLogContainsEverythingStandardLog: The debug log contains everything: the standard log, the errors, and every action (clicks, changed settings, pages opened, exchanges with the game and the services). Turn it on to report a problem, then turn it off: it grows quickly. API keys and typed text are never written to the logs.
settings.debugModeAlsoWritesDetailedLog: Debug mode: also writes a detailed log, in a separate file
settings.edchAlwaysRecordsWhatDoesStandard: EDCH always records what it does in a standard log (one file per start). Warnings and errors are also copied to a separate error log, created only when something goes wrong. Logs older than a week are deleted automatically, but the last 5 of each kind are always kept.
settings.edchOnlyOpensOnceLaunchingAgain: EDCH only opens once: launching it again brings the open window to the front. The window reopens where you left it.
settings.exeLnkShortcutMinedlauncherTipRight: An .exe, a .lnk shortcut, or MinEdLauncher. Tip: right-click the file → "Copy as path", then paste here (without the quotes).
settings.fromPhoneAlsoCopyPhoneS: From the phone, also copy to the phone's clipboard
settings.hiddenNotificationAreaEdchKeepsReading: Hidden in the notification area, EDCH keeps reading the journal: double-click its icon to reopen it, or right-click → Quit.
settings.hideNotificationAreaNextClock: Hide in the notification area (next to the clock)
settings.hideTabSoundStaysIfTicked: Hide the tab (the sound stays on if ticked)
settings.ignoresOlderFactionStatesBoomWar: Ignores older faction states (Boom, War…). 0 = no limit.
settings.launchEliteButtonTopScreenStarts: The "Launch Elite" button at the top of the screen starts the game, and shows when it's running. It works from the phone too.
settings.launcherChoiceFrontierMinedlauncher: A launcher of your choice (Frontier, MinEdLauncher…)
settings.linuxUpdatesArenTInstalledAutomatically: On Linux, updates aren't installed automatically: when a new version is out, EDCH opens the download page (AppImage, .deb, .rpm…).
settings.materialModuleEffectNamesFollowGame: Material, module and effect names follow the game's translation; control names stay as in the English game.
settings.minPopulationHighGradeEmissions: Min. population for High Grade Emissions
settings.moveWishlistItselfWhenGameApplies: Move the wishlist on by itself when the game applies a modification

support.helps: Support, even a little, helps to:
support.intro: EDCH is free, without ads, and will stay that way. It is designed, tested and maintained by CMDR MDLuffy, and developed with the help of the AI Claude (Anthropic).
support.reasonSigning: eventually pay for signing the application, so Windows stops flagging it.
support.reasonTime: keep time to test in game, fix bugs and follow Elite Dangerous updates;
support.reasonTools: pay for the tools that move the project forward (the subscription to the AI that writes the code with me);
support.thanks: It's also the best way to show the project matters to you. Thank you, and o7!
support.title: Support EDCH

missingData.title: Help complete the data
missingData.intro: When the game shows engineering EDCH's data doesn't know (an engineer doing a grade the data doesn't give them, a module or modification missing from the data), EDCH notes it here and in missing-data.txt, in the logs folder. Send the list in a GitHub issue: the data gets fixed for everyone.
missingData.privacy: The list holds no private data: engineers, modules, modifications, grades, dates and the game's version only.
missingData.afterSending: Once the issue is sent, delete missing-data.txt: the list starts again. EDCH does it by itself when it finds your issue on GitHub (it checks every 15 minutes).
missingData.waitingForIssue: Issue opened: waiting to find it on GitHub.

thargoids.howTypesAreKnown: The game's journal doesn't name the Thargoid you kill, nor those around you: EDCH recognises the type from the combat bond (scout 80,000 Cr, Glaive or Scythe 4.5 M, Cyclops 8 M, Orthrus 15 M, Basilisk 24 M, Medusa 40 M, Hydra 60 M). Scouts (Marauder, Berserker, Inciter, Regenerator…) all pay about the same bond and are counted together, and so are the Glaive and the Scythe.
